author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page listing each specialty with the veterinarians who hold it
summary: A read-only specialty view of the existing directory: list every stored specialty with the veterinarians holding it, each by full name. Reachable by URL alone, one page, no paging. Managing veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope (NG-2 unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html returns a page listing every specialty the clinic knows, each shown by its stored name
Each specialty lists the veterinarians who hold it, each by full name with given name first then family name (for example 'Helen Leary')
A veterinarian who holds no specialty does not appear anywhere on the page; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster
All specialties render on a single page with no pagination
No navigation entry and no link from any other page leads to the page; it is reachable by its address alone
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable, non-arbitrary order
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarians shown under it (narrowest reading of an open question)
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
A visible entry point (navigation entry or link from another page) — deferred to a possible follow-up request
notes: Inverse view of the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001). Full-name presentation and stable ordering mirror REQ-VET-001. The literal path /specialties.html is the interface contract for the implementer; PRD prose stays behavioral per the boundary rule. Open questions (empty specialty listed; sort key; entry-point deferral) recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions with narrowest-reading resolutions.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the inverse view of the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001) and reuses the vet feature package's established patterns wholesale: a feature-package @Controller depending directly on Spring Data repository interfaces (no service layer), a Thymeleaf server-rendered page under templates/, and a lookup-value repository mirroring owner/PetTypeRepository. No new architectural pattern, module, dependency, or bounded context is introduced (system-design.md Overview, Package Structure, Contracts). The one genuinely new element is a controller-level in-memory inversion of the Vet->Specialty @ManyToMany, which is a small adjustment to an existing shape rather than fresh ground -- hence 'minor'. No ADR is warranted: no hard-to-reverse or surprising decision, and the one small trade-off (new SpecialtyRepository vs. extending VetRepository) is resolved below on a concrete technical ground.
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html served by SpecialtyController -> view 'specialties/specialtyList'. No second (machine-readable) route -- the REQ-VET-001 /vets JSON route is a pending-removal defect, not a pattern to copy.

Data access: add SpecialtyRepository (extends JpaRepository<Specialty,Integer>) with a name-ordered query mirroring PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes(); enumerate ALL specialties from it, and load vets via the existing VetRepository.findAll() (already cached), then invert in the controller.

Inversion: for each ordered specialty, collect the vets whose Vet.getSpecialties() contains a specialty with the same id -- NOT via a Map keyed by the Specialty entity (BaseEntity has no equals/hashCode; identity keying would mismatch across two separate repository loads). Expose to the view as an ordered structure (e.g. a small view record or a LinkedHashMap keyed by specialty).

View reuses fragments/layout.html. Pass a menu selector that matches NO existing nav item (e.g. 'specialties') so no real menu entry is highlighted; do NOT add a navigation entry or cross-page link (entry-point deferral).

patterns.description: Lookup-value repository returning entities in name order via an explicit JPQL query -- the template for SpecialtyRepository (Specialty is a NamedEntity lookup value exactly like PetType).
Feature-package read controller: constructor-injected repository, GetMapping returning a view name with model attributes. Mirror its structure minus pagination.
Thymeleaf table page and full-name rendering (${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}); reuse the layout replace and the full-name expression, drop the pagination block.
@WebMvcTest controller slice pattern for asserting status, model attributes, and view name -- the shape SpecialtyControllerTests mirrors.

risks.risk: Empty-specialty case (a specialty held by no vet must still appear) is lost if the specialty set is derived from vets' specialties.
risks.mitigation: Enumerate specialties independently via SpecialtyRepository (name-ordered) and left-join vets in-memory; a specialty with no matching vet renders with an empty vet list. Cover with specialtyDirectoryListsASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian.

risks.risk: In-memory inversion keyed by the Specialty entity double-counts or drops entries because BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode (identity equality) and the two repository loads yield distinct instances.
risks.mitigation: Key the inversion by specialty id (Integer), not by the entity.

risks.risk: Adding a second no-arg cached method under @Cacheable("vets") on VetRepository would collide on the empty cache key with findAll(). This is the architectural reason to add a separate SpecialtyRepository (uncached) rather than extend VetRepository as the PRD file_targets suggested.
risks.mitigation: Use a new SpecialtyRepository without @Cacheable; leave VetRepository untouched.

risks.risk: New user-facing template strings would break REQ-LANG-002, enforced by the build-time test that walks templates and compares every locale bundle's keys.
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing keys where possible (#{specialties}, #{vets}/#{name}, #{none}); for any genuinely new key (e.g. a page heading or a 'no veterinarians' indicator) add it to ALL locale bundles under src/main/resources/messages/ before the gate runs.

risks.risk: Sort order under-specified (open question resolved at narrowest reading).
risks.mitigation: Specialties ordered by name (SpecialtyRepository ORDER BY name, consistent with Vet.getSpecialties() and PetTypeRepository); vets under each ordered by last name then first name via a controller Comparator. Stable and non-arbitrary, consistent with the full-name presentation.

notes: Verdict is 'minor' not 'new': every piece mirrors an existing pattern; the only novelty is inversion direction, a controller detail. Routing is unchanged from covered/new -- dispatch feature-implementer. Divergence from PRD file_targets: recommend a new SpecialtyRepository.java instead of touching VetRepository.java, for the cache-key collision reason above; VetRepository stays untouched. Read-only slice; NG-2 unchanged; no new dependency. Test approach mirrors VetControllerTests (@WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean the two repositories); note the tension with the project's no-mocks principle -- the existing controller-slice tests already use @MockitoBean, so mirroring is the consistent choice, but flag for test-reviewer whether a @SpringBootTest-with-H2 integration test is preferred instead. Post-implementation doc-sync should add SpecialtyController and SpecialtyRepository rows to system-design.md Contracts with Implements REQ-SPEC-001 (do not add them now -- source is authoritative and the code does not yet exist). No design-doc-autofix records present to audit.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Test data assigns exactly one vet per non-empty specialty (Helen Leary under radiology, Linda Douglas under surgery). The acceptance criterion 'Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable, non-arbitrary order' requires vet ordering within a specialty to be exercised, but with only one vet per specialty the Comparator in SpecialtyController is never stressed. A multi-vet scenario under one specialty is required to verify that sort order is correct and would be caught if broken.

The test uses @MockitoBean for SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository. Testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy states 'A new test reaches for a real implementation or a hand-written double first; a framework stub is a conscious exception, chosen only when neither fits.' H2 is on the test classpath and a @SpringBootTest approach with real repositories is feasible. The design-block explicitly flagged this tension and deferred the ruling to the test-reviewer. Ruling: the brief tolerates this pattern ('tolerated, not encouraged') and VetControllerTests establishes it as the codebase controller-slice precedent, but the brief's policy for new tests prefers real I/O. Request system-design-expert to issue a project-wide ruling on whether @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean is acceptable for new controller-slice tests, or whether @SpringBootTest + H2 is required.

Inline comment '// Every specialty appears in one response, ordered by name, with no pagination controls.' in specialtyDirectoryRendersAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage restates what the assertions already express. Testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure forbids prose that restates what the code already says.

Inline comment '// dentistry is held by no vet, yet still renders with a "none" indicator and no vet names.' in specialtyDirectoryListsASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian restates the test setup and assertion intent already clear from the code.

All five test method names follow a descriptive-behavioral pattern (e.g. 'specialtyDirectoryListsEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians') but deviate from the project's mandated BDD naming school 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}' (testing-principles.md § Test Naming, effective 2026-07-31). The PRD's test_names field prescribed these names without the 'the...Should' wrapper, creating an inconsistency with the naming school that governs the test file.

author: system-design-expert
answer: RULING on @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean for controller-slice tests. THIS-SLICE DECISION: SpecialtyControllerTests MAY keep the mirrored @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean pattern. It is NOT rewritten for REQ-SPEC-001. Basis: testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy does not strictly forbid the pattern. @WebMvcTest's MockMvc IS the one sanctioned mock -- 'the framework's in-process web test harness' standing in for HTTP transport, a system boundary (CLAUDE.md names it for this stack). The @MockitoBean stubs on SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository are framework stubs of internal collaborators, which the policy classes as 'tolerated, not encouraged': a conscious exception chosen when neither a real object nor a hand-written double fits. Here the controller-slice seam requires it -- @WebMvcTest does not load the JPA layer, so switching to real repositories means switching to @SpringBootTest + H2, i.e. abandoning the sanctioned web-slice harness. VetControllerTests establishes this as the settled codebase precedent for controller-slice tests. Narrowest-reading directive controls: rewriting to @SpringBootTest + H2 would expand REQ-SPEC-001 into a test-strategy migration, and the policy contains no strict prohibition that would compel it. FOLLOW-UP: none required as a separate item. No ADR is warranted -- the stance is already recorded in testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy; an ADR would fragment a single source of truth and no hard-to-reverse architectural decision is being taken. No testing-principles amendment is needed -- § Mocking Policy and § Test Pyramid already cover this exact tension and prescribe the direction. The genuine no-mocks improvement (extract the in-controller specialty->vet inversion into an independently unit-testable seam, per § Test Pyramid 'the ratio moves when logic moves') is an OPTIONAL future refactor, not a blocker and not owed by this slice. The test-reviewer's other findings stand and are the implementer's to resolve: the 'blocked' multi-vet ordering test (line 14) must still be added so the vet Comparator is exercised, and the autofix comment removals / BDD renames still apply -- this ruling does not waive them.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Six files, all net-new (zero deletions), confined to the vet feature package plus two doc rows; one read-only GET route, no sensitive paths, no dependency or config change.

semantic_surprise.note: Hunks do exactly what the description says: specialties enumerated independently so an empty one still renders, vets matched by id (correctly sidestepping the equals/hashCode-less BaseEntity trap), sorted family-then-given; no hidden behavior, no user input reaching a query.

test_adequacy.note: Six tests assert real rendered outcomes; the ordering test genuinely stresses the comparator with two same-family Jenkins vets (Rafael before Sharon) and would fail on a broken sort, and the empty-specialty and omission cases are covered -- not tautological.

reviewer_hedging.note: Final round is four unanimous approvals with empty findings; the earlier blocked doc-coherence and multi-vet-ordering findings were fixed and re-reviewed clean, and the lone escalate (stale CLAUDE.md task names) is an out-of-scope maintenance item, not a reservation about this change.

scope_deviation.note: Change matches REQ-SPEC-001's stated surface; the one divergence from PRD file_targets (new SpecialtyRepository instead of touching VetRepository) was design-block-sanctioned for a concrete cache-key-collision reason. Row shows zero design_revisions but the log holds one design-block and one test-strategy consultation; neither expanded scope.

rationale: All five facets clear on a reading of the hunks: a contained, read-only inverse-directory view whose one subtle correctness trap (BaseEntity identity keying) is handled by id-matching and whose comparator is genuinely exercised.
